applies_to: Graduate/doctoral students, researchers, and manuscripts submitted for publication
note: This file documents the key differences between APA-7 Professional format and Student/Basic format. All rules from the Student/Basic file apply unless overridden here.

elements: Title of paper (bold, centered, title case — 3-4 lines down from top margin)
Author note (contains ORCID iDs, disclosures, contact info)
Running head (shortened title, uppercase, max 50 characters)

running_head.format: Shortened version of the title in ALL CAPS
running_head.label_on_title_page: No label needed (APA-7 removed the 'Running head:' label from the title page)

author_note.placement: Bottom half of the title page
author_note.heading: 'Author Note' centered, bold
paragraphs: First paragraph: Author names and ORCID iDs
Second paragraph: Affiliation changes since the work was done
Third paragraph: Disclosures and acknowledgments (conflicts of interest, funding sources)
Fourth paragraph: Contact information (name, department, institution, address, email)

abstract.student_format_note: Not required for student papers unless instructor requests it
abstract.placement: Page 2, immediately after the title page
abstract.heading: 'Abstract' centered, bold, not italicized

format.no_indent: First line is NOT indented (flush left)

keywords.placement: Line below the abstract, indented 0.5 inch
keywords.label: 'Keywords:' in italics
keywords.format: Lowercase, separated by commas, no period at end

same_as_student_except.running_head: Required on every page (student papers do NOT have a running head)

font.note: Professional papers follow journal submission guidelines if applicable

order: Title page (with running head and author note)
Body (title repeated on first line, bold, centered)
Footnotes (if collected on a separate page instead of at bottom of pages)
Tables (each on its own page, if not embedded)
Figures (each on its own page, if not embedded)

citations.note: All citation rules are identical between student and professional formats

summary_of_key_rules.three_or_more_authors: First author et al. (Year) every time
summary_of_key_rules.cite_once_per_paragraph: If reader can clearly tell subsequent sentences come from the same source

heading_levels.level_1: Centered, bold, title case — content on next line
heading_levels.level_2: Left-aligned, bold, title case — content on next line
heading_levels.level_3: Left-aligned, bold, italic, title case — content on next line
heading_levels.level_4: Indented 0.5 inch, bold, title case, period — content continues on same line
heading_levels.level_5: Indented 0.5 inch, bold, italic, title case, period — content continues on same line

reference_list.note: Identical formatting rules to student format
reference_list.heading: Centered, bold ('References')

title_page.student: No running head, no author note. Lists course number, instructor name, due date.
title_page.professional: Has running head, has author note with ORCID/disclosures/contact. Lists institutional affiliation(s).

abstract.student: Not required unless instructor requests it
abstract.professional: Required. Page 2, 150-250 words, with keywords line.

running_head.professional: Required on every page, ALL CAPS, max 50 characters

author_note.professional: Required on title page. Contains ORCID iDs, disclosures, funding, and contact info.

tables_and_figures_placement.student: Typically embedded in the text near first mention
tables_and_figures_placement.professional: May be embedded or collected at the end after references (per journal requirements)

person_usage.student: Avoid first and second person unless assignment permits it
person_usage.professional: APA encourages first person ('I' for single author, 'we' for multiple) for clarity and directness

shared_rules_reference.note: The following rules are identical across both formats. See apa7_student_basic_rules.json for full details.
categories: All citation and in-text citation rules
